title: Reading Career Paths & Job Requirements
summary: Learn how to read career information and job descriptions by separating duties, required qualifications, preferred qualifications, credentials, experience, and working conditions.
objectives: Identify major parts of a job description.
Distinguish required qualifications from preferred qualifications.
Recognize when a career requirement must be verified with an authoritative source.

vocab.def: A responsibility or task normally associated with a role.
A condition an employer or governing authority identifies as necessary for a role or opportunity.
A qualification that may strengthen a candidate but is not necessarily required.
A condition that must be satisfied before entering a program, activity, training route, or role.

sections.heading: Job descriptions contain different kinds of information
sections.body: A posting may describe duties, schedule, work environment, education, experience, skills, credentials, physical expectations, location, and application requirements.

sections.heading: Required and preferred are not the same
sections.body: A required qualification is presented as necessary. A preferred qualification may make an applicant stronger but is not automatically a condition of eligibility.

sections.heading: Some requirements come from outside the employer
sections.body: Certain occupations may involve licenses, certifications, registrations, age requirements, training rules, or other external requirements. These should be checked against authoritative sources.

sections.heading: Read for the real next step
sections.body: Career research should answer what the role actually requires today and what step would move you closer, rather than assuming every interesting occupation is immediately available.

practice.prompt: A job posting lists two years of experience under 'preferred qualifications.' Is that automatically the same as a mandatory requirement?
practice.answer: No. Preferred and required qualifications should be interpreted separately.

practice.prompt: A website says a career requires a state license. What should you do before building your plan around that claim?
practice.answer: Check the requirement against the appropriate authoritative state or occupational source.

quiz.question: What is the best way to interpret a job posting?
options: Separate duties, required qualifications, preferred qualifications, and verified external requirements
Assume every listed item is legally required
Assume an introductory course satisfies every qualification
quiz.answer: Separate duties, required qualifications, preferred qualifications, and verified external requirements

lab.objective: Analyze simulated job postings and identify duties, required qualifications, preferred qualifications, credentials, experience expectations, and questions that require verification.

reflectionPrompt: Why can understanding the difference between required and preferred qualifications change how you approach an opportunity?
